title: The Secret Garden
description: Maya and Kai solve the mysteries of a glowing biodome on a distant moon, learning to check evidence as the five rings illuminate.

pages.title: The Thirty-Day Tree
lines: Seven seconds after leaving Earth, the Ninja explorers stood beneath unfamiliar stars.
Across the moon's silver valley, a glowing biodome rose like a glass mountain.
Inside, one golden-fruited tree stretched higher than every other plant.
Maya checked her wrist screen, which displayed a surprising measurement : TREE AGE: 30 DAYS.
"A tree that big in one month?" Kai asked.
Maya zoomed in and spotted five glowing rings around its trunk.
The rings lit up one after another, almost as though the garden were inviting them inside.
"I think," Maya said, "we've found our next mystery."
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 1: The Thirty-Day Tree

pages.title: Five Glowing Clues
lines: The doors opened onto towers of strawberries, bright flowers, and streams beneath clear walkways.
A cheerful robot rolled forward and introduced itself as Luma, the garden's guide.
Above its head appeared a hologram showing the giant tree surrounded by five symbols.
"Each symbol hides a clue," Luma explained, "and together they reveal the garden's secret."
Kai noticed a glowing indicator pointing toward some lettuce.
"We have to solve this ourselves?" he asked.
"You get to," Luma answered, its eyes flashing blue.
Maya followed the light, determined to discover whether the thirty-day tree was real.
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 2: Five Glowing Clues

pages.title: Roots Without Dirt
lines: Beneath the lettuce, white roots dangled in clear water instead of soil.
"Somebody forgot the dirt," Kai whispered, but Maya was already examining the flowing channels.
Luma called the method hydroponics .
The water carried nutrients .
Maya traced a channel until it disappeared beneath the giant tree.
"So roots can get what they need without soil," she said.
The first ring turned green, displaying: ROOTS NEED THE RIGHT CONDITIONS.
Kai grinned, but Maya noticed that the tree's roots were hidden behind a wall.
"Interesting," she said, "but we still haven't seen what's underneath that tree."
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 3: Roots Without Dirt

pages.title: A Sky Built by Scientists
lines: The next light led them upstairs beneath rows of red, blue, and white lamps.
"It's like someone built a second sky," Kai said.
Luma explained photosynthesis .
Different colors belonged to the visible spectrum .
Maya watched the lamps above the giant tree brighten in a carefully timed pattern.
"You can give plants useful light even when sunlight is limited," she realized.
The second ring flashed green, but a narrow beam swept across the trunk and stopped at a glass panel.
On the panel appeared another message: LOOK CLOSER AT THE WATER.
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 4: A Sky Built by Scientists

pages.title: The Water’s Return Trip
lines: Behind the panel, clear pipes twisted overhead like a transparent maze.
Kai watched water move through a repeating circulation .
Some returning water passed through filtration .
Elsewhere, cool surfaces collected moisture released by leaves.
"So the garden catches water and uses some again," Maya said.
"Yes, though we still replace what the system loses," Luma replied.
The third ring glowed green as a pipe beside the tree lit up from bottom to top.
At its highest point, the ninjas spotted a small silver robot waiting beside the branches.
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 5: The Water’s Return Trip

pages.title: The Tiny Garden Detectives
lines: The robot floated from leaf to leaf, recording information without touching the fruit.
Luma said its sensors checked temperature, light, and moisture.
The garden also used automation .
Kai watched another robot adjust a lamp after receiving a measurement.
"It's like the whole garden is paying attention," he said.
Maya examined a screen and discovered that the giant tree had arrived exactly thirty days earlier.
Before she could mention it, the fourth ring flashed green and sparkling golden mist filled the room.
Luma rolled toward the tree and announced, "One clue remains."
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 6: The Tiny Garden Detectives

pages.title: The Golden Rain
lines: Fine droplets shimmered above the branches, turning ordinary water into a curtain of gold.
"It's beautiful," Maya said, catching a drop on her glove.
Luma explained humidity and showed how the garden controlled it.
Careful conservation helped the system collect and reuse water.
Kai counted four green rings and one still silver.
"We know about roots, light, water, and robots," he said, "so what's missing?"
Maya looked from the mist to the pipes, then toward the hidden roots.
"Maybe the answer isn't another machine," she whispered.
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 7: The Golden Rain

pages.title: The Fifth Ring
lines: Maya called up the hologram and placed the four discoveries together.
The pipes fed the roots, the lamps lit the leaves, and the sensors helped control both.
"They work together," she said, "instead of working alone."
Luma called this integration and optimization .
The fifth ring burst into green light, and the hologram displayed: MYSTERY SOLVED.
Kai cheered, but Maya held up her hand.
"Not quite," she said, pointing to the original message on her wrist.
"We've explained how the garden works, but have we proved this huge tree grew in thirty days?"
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 8: The Fifth Ring

pages.title: The Number That Changed Everything
lines: Luma opened the hidden panel, revealing a photograph of the tree arriving on a transport platform.
It was already tall, with thick branches and golden fruit beginning to form.
"Thirty days in this garden," Maya realized, "not thirty days since the seed sprouted!"
The tree had undergone transplantation after years of cultivation .
Kai laughed.
"We solved five clues, but the biggest mystery was what the number meant!"
Luma changed the display to read: TIME IN BIODOME: 30 DAYS.
Maya smiled at the towering branches.
"Good scientists don't just collect facts," she said.
"They check what those facts actually tell them."
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 9: The Number That Changed Everything

pages.title: The Garden of Tomorrow
lines: At sunset, Luma projected future cities with vegetable gardens climbing their buildings.
It described sustainability .
The ninjas saw how innovation could help grow food in cities, deserts, and spacecraft.
"Our biggest discovery wasn't a magical tree," Kai said as the dome glowed behind them.
"It was learning how real science works," Maya replied.
She saved the corrected measurement beside a picture of the five glowing rings.
Then Luma showed them one final image: a small garden floating inside a spacecraft far from any planet.
"Now," Luma asked, "how would you grow food where there is almost no gravity?"
The ninjas exchanged excited looks, already imagining their next adventure.
pages.alt: Original Secret Garden cinematic illustration 10: The Garden of Tomorrow
